HomePage.title: NekoLog
HomePage.tagline: Logging for JavaScript and TypeScript applications, front-end and back-end.
HomePage.lede: SDKs that batch and send what your application already writes, an ingestion API, ClickHouse for storage, background jobs for alerts, and a dashboard to read it all back.
HomePage.status: Version 1.0, by invitation. There is no open sign-up: an invitation gives you the SDK for your stack and a dashboard login.
HomePage.readLabel: And read it back, from anywhere

sdks.title: 12 SDKs over one core
sdks.body: Browser, Node, React, Next, Express, Fastify, Hono, NestJS, plus bridges for pino and winston, a CLI and a bundler plugin. One implementation underneath, so they cannot drift.

privacy.title: Privacy before the network call
privacy.body: Passwords, tokens, card numbers and CPFs are stripped inside your process, before anything is sent — and again on the server, from a closed list of patterns per environment.

search.title: A search language, not a substring
search.body: level:error service:api @status>=500 "timeout". Parsed, bounded and compiled to parameters, never interpolated into SQL.

issues.title: Errors grouped at ingestion
issues.body: The fingerprint is computed where the event arrives, so grouping never needs a second pass over the table. An issue that was fixed and happens again reopens; one you ignored stays quiet.

alerts.title: Alerts that fail safe
alerts.body: Every rule of an environment is measured in one query. A measurement that failed never resolves a firing alert, and a webhook address is checked for SSRF when it is saved and again when it is used.

otlp.title: OpenTelemetry, if you prefer
otlp.body: POST /v1/otlp/logs takes OTLP/HTTP and converts it before anything else runs, so an OTLP record goes through exactly the same validation and redaction as a native one.

model.title: What runs where
model.body: NekoLog is proprietary software, and you run almost none of it. The SDK goes into your application; everything behind it is ours to operate.
model.line: There is nothing to deploy, nothing to keep up at three in the morning, and no database of yours to size. When the ingestion needs more room, that is our problem.
model.yoursBody: One SDK, installed into your application. It never throws into your app, carries no dependencies, and strips sensitive values before the first network call.
model.oursBody: Ingestion, storage, retention, error grouping, alerting, exports, and the dashboard you read them in — kept up, backed up and watched.

data.title: What it does with your data
data.ip: The IP address is never written. Not hashed, not truncated — the row carries the country, and a test fails if an address header reaches storage.
data.client: Sensitive values are stripped inside your process, after your own beforeSend hook, so the hook cannot undo it.
data.server: And again on the server, from a closed list of named patterns. You cannot supply a regular expression, because a third party's regex on the hot path of a server with a 10 ms CPU budget per request is a denial of service you write for yourself.
data.url: A click breadcrumb records the selector, never the element's text. page.url drops the query string, because reset tokens live there.

numbers.title: Measured, not claimed
numbers.deps: @nekolog-io/core has zero runtime dependencies, by contract — and every package ships a CycloneDX bill of materials built from the lockfile, so a dependency arriving there fails the release.
numbers.size: The browser SDK does not meet its own size budget. The target was 5 kB gzip; init is 12.05 kB. Most of that is the privacy pipeline, which is not optional. The miss is written down rather than rounded away.
numbers.cpu: The biggest batch the protocol allows did not fit the budget: 500 events cost 10.8 ms of CPU against a 10 ms ceiling on a core the database shares. The client's default batch is 200 events now, and a test guards the budget in CI.
numbers.runtimes: Node 22, 24 and 26, Bun, Deno, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit run the suite on every pull request — against the built package, not the source.
